items.summary: Roundabouts, merchant republics, and dark fantasy roguelikes aren't budging their release plans.

content.v: Though it might seem hard to believe given its inescapability, not everyone is going to be playing GTA 6 next week. Some might be waiting for its eventual PC release (whenever that ends up being). Others might simply be unwilling to spend over a thousand dollars on a console just to enjoy the privilege.

Most publishers and developers releasing a videogame this season, however, have opted to vacate the GTA 6 blast radius—but not all of them. If you're looking for something new to play next week, you'll be pleased to know there are some brave games still launching on Steam. Here are some options to consider if you aren't dropping into Vice City:
Crusader Kings 3: Silk and Silver
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/vX4bunbXqfUKgihhRktUQT-1920-80.jpg

If you're a CK3 player—and you should be; it's number eight on our Top 100 list for a reason—then Paradox's next expansion should be on your radar. While everyone else is focused on Grand Theft Auto, you could be engaging in the grandest theft of all: Commerce.

Silk and Silver is all about mercantilism: Merchant families can jockey for trade route monopolies and use their wealth to lobby for influence, while new Republic governments offer patrician dynasties a venue to vie for dominance in the constitutional Assembly—potentially forming commercial or military pacts with other Republics. It's also got a lot of Italian content in it. Everyone loves Italian content.
Crusader Kings 3: Silk and Silver launches on November 17.
Spirit Crossing
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/mvFBGwdcSkyWc6CSUSmHCZ-1920-80.jpg

Among the cozier offerings arriving on Steam during GTA 6 week, Spirit Crossing is a building, crafting, and decorating MMO set in a world seemingly populated entirely by art students and befriendable spirits.

Borrowing a page from Sky: Children of the Light, it's only as much of an MMO as you want it to be: other players are only fully visible in your world if you mutually choose to engage with one another. Otherwise, you're free to roam its pastel soulscape and build out your own little corner of paradise solo for as long as you prefer.
Spirit Crossing launches on November 16.
Harma
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/cL7fraYVhVrnWnkWrbopje-1920-80.jpg

Listen. I know. It's 2026. I feel the same suspicions that you do when you see a game with full-on pixel illustrations like this on Steam nowadays. But the developers of Harma insist that it's "developed entirely by human creators and does not contain any contents or assets generated by AI tools." Which is good, because it looks neat, and I want to believe.

It's a roguelike deckbuilder that has both a story-driven campaign and a replayable "Dimensional Rift" mode, which should provide plenty of opportunity to continue admiring the work of its pixel artists. Assuming there were, in fact, pixel artists. They wouldn't lie to me, right? Please?
Harma launches in early access on November 16.
Melvor Idle 2
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/3sLFtV5A9xqevkMZwHyUoj-1920-80.jpg

Melvor Idle is for one of the most particular types of guys, and whether or not you're one of them should be clarified as soon as I say this sentence: Melvor Idle 2 is like Old School RuneScape with all the parts that aren't a skill grind stripped away. It's 100% gathering items so you can get better at gathering items so you can gather better items. It's pure, uncut clicking and waiting as numbers go up.

It's so thoroughly for RuneScape guys that, after the success of the first Melvor Idle, Jagex brought the operation under its publishing wing. If that's for you, I'm not judging. In many ways, you're living a more honest life than I am.
Melvor Idle 2 launches in early access on November 17.
Trafficity
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/RqBPhHFroaHbCVRQcEHSr-1920-80.jpg

If you do not yet acknowledge the awesome power of the roundabout, it is time to learn. Trafficity is a game about traffic. There are cars, and they must go places. But only so many cars can go to one place at once.
This is the crux on which our world is both built and broken.

And now it is yours to solve—using a toolkit of gridless road design tools, fully-customizable traffic lights, and dynamic interchange simulation. Somewhere, in another game, your uncouth lessers are disrupting this great task with the stealing and crashing of your vehicular charges. But now, you answer to a higher calling. The traffic must flow.
Trafficity launches on November 16.

items.title: 不喜欢游戏中的人工智能？ Crimson Desert 工作室 Pearl Abyss 并不关心：它正在“在我们的整个开发流程中”扩大人工智能的使用
items.summary: Pearl Abyss apologized for the presence of AI-generated art in Crimson Desert earlier this year, but it's not

content.v: Earlier this year, Pearl Abyss apologized for the presence of AI-generated art in Crimson Desert—not because it had used generative AI, mind, but because players saw it. And it seems like the odds we might see more of it in the future are going up, as the studio said in its Q3 2026 earnings letter (via Eurogamer ) that it will be going even deeper on AI-powered development in the future.

The first reference to AI comes midway through the letter: "While we previously validated game systems only after implementing them manually, we now utilize AI to rapidly validate diverse design concepts prior to actual implementation," it states. "This enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed."

The studio immediately clarified, though, that AI "serves strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity," and that gameplay and content development "remain fully driven by our development team."

The future will see more of the same, with the same caveats. "We are integrating AI technologies to enhance development productivity and overall quality," Pearl Abyss writes. "AI is being utilized across various stages of development—including the automation of repetitive tasks, content creation support, and test optimization—and we are expanding its implementation throughout our entire development pipeline.

"We view AI not as a substitute for human developers, but as a tool to elevate development efficiency and quality. We will continue to expand our application of AI to deliver higher-fidelity games to the market more expeditiously."

That essentially repeats what Pearl Abyss said in February when players discovered the presence of generative AI art in Crimson Desert : It acknowledged that "some 2D visual props" had been created by AI during the early stages of development, but said they were supposed to be replaced "following final work and review by our art and development teams, with work that aligned with our quality standards and creative direction."

The studio also admitted that it had not "clearly disclosed our use of AI" in the development process, and promised to be more transparent about it in the future. This letter certainly could be seen as a step in that direction.
Pearl Abyss also said it aims to release DokeV, the " weird GTA: Babies game " revealed in 2021, sometime in the second half of 2028.

items.summary: We ranked all four Magic: The Gathering Star Trek Commander precons—from Picard’s Federation Fleet to We Are t

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/07/17/star-trek-commander-deck-deal-amazon-ign-1784274048211.png
Magic: The Gathering’s Star Trek set is finally here, closing out a particularly packed release schedule for Wizards of the Coast’s long-running TCG.

Star Trek is the seventh set of the year, and it brings with it another four Commander decks to take this year’s total to 17. Still, as we all know, not all decks are created equal - so which one comes out on top?
The Klingons or the Borg? Picard or Spock? Here’s our ranking.
Before We Begin

If you’re picking up all four decks because you’re a Trekkie, or you just love new precons, Amazon has cut the price of the bundle again to just $224.97 , basically offsetting the “Universes Beyond” tax.
That’s not the Collector Editions, though: Those are well over $100 each. They include the same cards, but all in foil.
Ranking Magic’s Star Trek Decks
Federation Fleet
Color Identity: Jeskai (blue, red, white)
Reprints of note: Alhammarret’s Archive
Magic loves to put heroic precons in Jeskai colors, and Federation Fleet is no exception - although it does come last in our ranking.

Its primary Commander, Jean-Luc Picard, Luminary, is a four-cost 2/4 that draws you cards as you play historic permanents, which then triggers the Seek Out mechanic. This lets you charge up a Spacecraft and add a counter to another target creature.
It’s not that it’s not a fun, cohesive deck, but it’s definitely just not as interesting on a mechanical level as the others in this set.
Klingon Fury
Color Identity: Mardu (white, black, red)
Reprints of note: Sword of Light, Shadow and World at War
Worf, Defiant Commander is in charge of the Klingon Fury deck, which makes use of the Battlefront mechanic to encourage players to play aggressively.

Worf creates Klingon Warrior tokens when it hits the battlefield, and the more opponents you attack on your turn, the more cards you exile from the top of your library, which you can play until the end of your next turn.
It’s not quite cheating big creatures into play, but it should mean you’re well-stocked with options as long as you keep Worf around.
Landing Party
Color Identity: Bant (green, white, blue)
Reprints of note: Ancient Greenwarden, Scute Swarm, Exploration, Heroic Intervention
Commander Spock is the logical choice for a Commander in Bant colors, and Wizards of the Coast has made it so here (sorry).

Landing Party’s Strange New Worlds mechanic helps play cards more quickly if you’ve got more differently named lands in the set. Given there are 40 in the deck, that should be easily done, but this deck also gives you a big bundle of non-basic lands in Bant colors if you need them.

Captain Kirk, Boldly Going, is another Commander option. William Shatner himself is a 3/4 with vigilance who powers up your Spacecraft cards. The card can also grab you land cards or the Enterprise from your library or graveyard.
We Are The Borg
Color Identity: Esper (white, blue, black)
Reprints of note: Toxic Deluge, Unwinding Clock, Morphic Pool

Our top pick for the Commander precons in the Star Trek set is We Are The Borg . Standing somewhere between artifact synergies and a “what’s yours is mine” deck, The Borg Queen pumps artifact creatures and also assimilates cards to your side of the battlefield.

Unwinding Clock is a very welcome reprint here since it fits nicely into just about any other artifact strategy, and Locutus of Borg can help you pull even more Borg to the table. It’s a deck that’s likely to get out of hand pretty quickly, and for that reason, it’s our top pick.

For more on Magic: The Gathering, check out some of our favorite Commander decks of all time , as well as the latest on reprints of the sought-after Universes Beyond: Warhammer 40K decks , and the most valuable cards to look out for in the new Star Trek Universes Beyond set .

items.title: “实体”GTA 6 副本可能容易受到一个非常愚蠢但严重的骗局的影响
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 ditched traditional discs for its "physical" launch, with Rockstar's game being sold as a d

content.v: Grand Theft Auto 6 ditched traditional discs for its "physical" launch, with Rockstar's game being sold as a digital code-in-box at retailers beginning this week. However, it appears a packaging choice may have accidentally left the game vulnerable to thieves--assuming they have a flashlight.

As shared on the forum ResetEra , users who received a physical version of Grand Theft Auto 6, at least in PEGI regions, report that the game's download code is printed directly on the inside of the cover rather than on a card or separate insert. When a flashlight is focused on the cover from the outside of the closed game case, the download code is visible in reverse.
In other words, there's a serious risk people could go into a store, do this trick, redeem the code, and leave the poor soul who actually buys the game off the shelf without GTA 6.

At this time, the trick does not seem to work on North American copies of GTA 6, as the code is intentionally obscured. Why Rockstar would not use this strategy on all regions is unclear. We've reached out to Rockstar for an explanation and will update this post if and when we receive a response.

If you happen to get your GTA 6 code stolen after paying $80 , you can at least sleep soundly knowing that the thief can't play the game yet. Code-in-box copies, as well as digital preorders, all unlock for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19.

items.title: EA 以 550 亿美元私有化后，GTA 6 所有者 Take-Two 无意出售自己
items.summary: Recently, the gaming giant Electronic Arts was taken private in a $55 billion sale to an investor consortium l

content.v: Recently, the gaming giant Electronic Arts was taken private in a $55 billion sale to an investor consortium led by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. Could GTA 6 owner Take-Two be the next big company that gets acquired? Don't bet on it, CEO Strauss Zelnick says.
Speaking to David Rubenstein , Zelnick said Take-Two's business results have proven that it "can do very well as an independent company."
He said Take-Two's business is already "at scale" and healthy enough financially with a "terrific balance sheet," as he put it.
"We are not in a place where we need to be part of a bigger organization to be competitive. And in the entertainment business, scale matters," he said.

Zelnick said companies that do less than a billion in annual revenue might have issues with developing, marketing, and distributing games at scale. Not only that, but companies that don't generate a lot of money might not be able to survive the realities of the creative business, in which sometimes your product flops.

"But once you're over a billion dollars in annual revenue, and we're way beyond that point. Our guidance is $8 billion to $8.2 billion this fiscal year, additional scale doesn't seem to help you succeed."

In early 2008, Electronic Arts privately pursued a buyout of Take-Two, but after the GTA and BioShock company rejected it, EA went public in an attempt to get a deal done. Later that year, EA abandoned its plans to try to buy Take-Two after the GTA company said it was worth more and EA refused to increase its bid.
In 2019, it was rumored that Sony was attempting to buy Take-Two, but that was ultimately deemed to be unconfirmed market chatter and not a formal bid .

Take-Two has a market cap of more than $42 billion, and that is expected to grow in the year ahead , so it would seemingly take a lot of money to convince Take-Two to sell. Going forward, Zelnick has teased that new GTA games could release even faster , and that could be a positive for the company's financials.
GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Preloading is underway now, and that's good news because the game has a massive file size .

items.title: A survival game we once called 'Stalker and Tarkov's alien baby' is closing down less than a year after launch
items.summary: Pioner seemed headed in the right direction when it went into early access in late 2025, but it all went wrong

content.v: Pioner, a survival-shooter we said looked like " Stalker and Tarkov's alien baby " when we first laid eyes on it in 2021, is ending development and closing down. In an announcement posted today on Steam, developer GFAGames said further work on the game and continued operation of its servers requires more money, and it just doesn't have any.

"Over the past few months, we have been in talks with existing and potential partners about investment and new ways of working together that would allow us to preserve the project and the team," the studio wrote.
"We were unable to agree on the funding needed to continue the project. The studio no longer has sufficient funds of its own to continue development and keep the servers running."

Pioner looked promising when it turned up at the PC Gaming Show in 2021: A mash-up of Stalker, Metro, and Escape From Tarkov that featured both a singleplayer campaign and online co-op and PvP survival action, all of it built around late Soviet-era technology.

It launched into early access in December 2025 and worked its way to a peak concurrent player count of 1,686 on Steam a few months later—not huge, but far from catastrophic, and trending in the right direction.

Those numbers tailed off badly over the summer, though, as the dev team struggled with technical issues and updates came at a much slower pace than promised. August saw player counts collapse almost completely, and by mid-September only a couple dozen people were still playing.

Numerous replies to the shutdown announcement call for refunds to be issued, but GFAGames hasn't commented on those demands at this point. It also hasn't said when the game will actually be taken offline—I've reached out to ask and will update if I receive a reply.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/13/rainbow-six-vegas-1794596888042.png
Ubisoft has reportedly given a new entry in the Rainbow Six: Vegas series the green light and a codename.

Details on a long-awaited (and unexpected) return to a fan-favorite corner of the Rainbow Six universe come from an Insider Gaming report. The publisher is said to have given its Ubisoft Montreal team the go-ahead to begin work on a new Vegas installment, with two other projects reportedly also in the works there.

Rainbow Six: Vegas started with the release of the original game in 2006 before it returned for a sequel in 2008. Whether the new game will be called Rainbow Six: Vegas 3 or something else is unclear, though the site's sources say it's expected to be more like the former rather than something like a remake. It also stated that it's being worked on with the apt codename, "Spades."

That's just one of the three games the Montreal studio is reportedly working on. The report wasn't able to confirm much about the remaining projects but said one source suggested at least one other game is planned to take place in the Rainbow Six universe in some capacity.

The Rainbow Six franchise as a whole existed long before popular entries like Rainbow Six Siege or even the Vegas series. Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six traces all the way back to the late '90s but has splintered into a wide variety of gameplay experiences and offerings. Siege is no doubt the most well-known iteration today thanks to how Ubisoft has supported its tactical gameplay since its 2015 launch, but the most recent entry actually arrived in 2022 with Rainbow Six Extraction .

Despite nearly 20 years passing since the last Vegas game, it's remained a beloved corner of the universe for many. IGN gave the original game a 7.6/10 when it launched for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. We then gave the sequel's limited edition release an 8.4/10 .

Ubisoft seems to be still in the early stages of its unannounced Rainbow Six: Vegas continuation, so don't expect to see it launch for at least a few more years. While that may mean we'll have passed the 20-year mark since the last game, we hopefully won't have to wait quite as long to learn more about it. Until then, it's best to keep expectations low while the publisher keeps its cards close to its chest.

Meanwhile, we do know about a few other projects Ubisoft has up its sleeve. Rainbow Six Tactics , for example, was announced in August and will launch sometime next year. A Splinter Cell remake is also in the works, even if it's been a while since we heard from it .

content.v: Microsoft has issued an apology for the global services outage that began on November 12, which disrupted access to Microsoft 365 products for governments, hospitals, schools, and businesses around the world. The corporation says that neither AI nor malicious actors were at fault, but that the outage occurred as a result of an underlying infrastructural issue introduced during a network upgrade.

"We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously," Microsoft said. "We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services."

We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services.This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration.We will provide a full post-incident report once our review is complete. November 13, 2026

While popular speculation has been eager to attribute the outage to vibe-coding—and I can't blame anyone for speculating, considering Microsoft's push for company-wide AI adoption —the corporation says the outage was "a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents." It's unclear whether another word was meant to follow "cyber." I'm just telling you what the company wrote.

"The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change," Microsoft said, casually brutalizing the syntax of causality. "We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions."
Microsoft acknowledged that the restoration of service was slower than many might have hoped, but said that it brought services back online gradually to ensure stability.

Even if AI wasn't to blame for this week's outage, it's tempting to wonder whether any of the 10,000 employees Microsoft laid off in 2023 as part of its ongoing cost-cutting strategy might have known how to avoid the costly hiccup. Or any of the 6,000 employees it laid off in May 2025. Or the 9,000 it laid off that July. Or the 4,800 it laid off a year later, including 1,600 at Xbox with another 1,600 to follow. Or the 60,000 employees it extended voluntary buyout offers to last month.
Ah, well. No way to know. Microsoft said it will provide a more detailed incident report once its internal review of the outage is complete.

items.summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19, and it's expected to be a gigantic commercial success,

content.v: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19, and it's expected to be a gigantic commercial success, but just how big will the launch be? Investor's Business Daily compiled data from a series of analyst reports about the game and its owner, Take-Two, and the consensus is that it's going to be a juggernaut.

In terms of sales, Brian Pitz of BMO Capital Markets said GTA 6 could sell 55 million copies during Take-Two's fiscal 2027, which ends on March 31, 2027. He said the game could sell 45 million units alone during the game's launch quarter, which is well ahead of the estimates of 34.2 million that IBD compiled.

"This is an outlier in every respect," Circana's Mat Piscatella told the publication. "There have been some big game launches in the past, but nothing quite at this scale, not only in terms of the investment, but in terms of the anticipation. It's in its own league."

GTA 6 is launching with an $80 standard edition and a $100 Ultimate Edition. Raymond James analyst Andrew Marok said he's forecasting 50 million unit sales for the fiscal year 2027, and that the blended average selling price will be close to $90. According to Sensor Tower, early data suggested preorders were skewing toward the $100 edition, but by launch, it could be around 50/50 .

Matthew Cost of Morgan Stanley, meanwhile, said if GTA 6 does indeed have strong sales out of the gate, this could create a "large potential audience" for the next iteration of GTA Online . Rockstar has not said anything yet about an online mode for GTA 6, but given the huge success of GTA Online for GTA 5, it's all but guaranteed that GTA 6 will incorporate online multiplayer as well.

Cost said this is a big deal for investors and may represent "the next major catalyst" for Take-Two's stock price. Take-Two's share price is down about 10% so far in 2026 , and currently trades around $228/share..

A new version of GTA Online for GTA 6 would no doubt feature microtransactions and other ways to spend more money, and that could be frustrating for fans but great news for investors who want to see bigger returns.

D.A. Davidson analyst Wyatt Swanson said Take-Two's share price could surge to $300 in part because he believes Rockstar will release a PC edition of GTA 6 and usher in GTA Online 2.0. These releases would "enable structurally higher margins" for Take-Two, he said.

According to Sensor Tower, GTA 6 has already sold 12 million copies and generated $1.2 billion in revenue . GTA 5, meanwhile, took 72 hours to clear $1 billion in revenue --GTA 6 reached that a week before release, apparently.
GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

Macca and Friends, as the show is known, follows the adventures of a gang of anthropomorphic Floridian—Leonidan, I suppose—animals as they try to find their way in the world, accompanied to some extent by a beefed-up cop. Rockstar hasn't said anything about the show, but this isn't the first appearance of Macca: A Macca and Friends mural appeared in a real-life BurgerShot that was set up in Miami's Kaseya Center in October, and a billboard for the show was erected in Miami as well.

In that light, is it hard to believe they may have created an entire animated series for GTA 6?
It might just be another blast from the GTA marketing machine—Rockstar is also literally renting the Miami Heat to promote its game, after all. At this point I don't think anything's off the table.

items.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever has been in the wild for one week, and now we have all kinds of stats to sink our t

content.v: World of Warcraft: Forever has been in the wild for one week, and now we have all kinds of stats to sink our teeth into as they relate to the most popular races, classes, and faction in the latest version of developer Blizzard's MMORPG.

Forever launched November 4, becoming the biggest launch in WoW history by concurrent and returning players. Aside from that fact, Blizzard hasn't shared additional information on exactly how many characters have been made or what classes are most popular.
For that, we turn to Raider.IO , a WoW stat-tracking website more commonly used in the modern version of the game to provide rankings and details related to raids and Mythic+ progression.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/WoW-Forever-RaiderIO-stats.jpg?w=636

According to the site, close to 3.9 million characters have been created across all regions and rulesets so far. Around 48% of those characters are on the Alliance, with nearly 52% being on the Horde.

The most popular two races aren't all that surprising--undead and humans. Despite being the most boring choice imaginable, humans have always been a popular choice in WoW Classic thanks to their strong passives and the ability to be most classes. In Forever, they currently make up 37% of the Alliance population. Undead, on the other hand, are getting a massive boost from being the only Horde race to currently have access to Paladin. They make up nearly 40% of the Horde.
It won't shock you to learn then that Paladin is Forever's most-played class, with undead Paladin being the most-played race-and-class combo.

Skyborne elves are WoW's newest playable race, available to both factions. Around 10% of all characters are Skyborne, and faction-wise they are fairly even. Around 10% of Skyborne are Alliance and close to 11% are on the Horde. Consdiering how popular blood elves are in other versions of the game, the number of Skyborne feels low by comparison, though the fact they cost $30 to access probably has something to do with that.

As for what rulesets are most popular, the normal (PvE) server is far and away the biggest, with over 2 million characters. The PvP ruleset isn't too far behind with around 1.5 million characters. Those two rulesets dwarf the size of the game's two RP rulesets, which combined have around 250,000 players.

With the exception of standard RP, every ruleset has a larger Horde population, a subject Blizzard recently commented on officially. In a forum post , Blizzard announced its goal is for PvP servers to be as close to 50/50 faction balance as possible, and would be placing restrictions on creating Horde characters on PvP rulesets in an effort to make that a reality.

"World of Warcraft: Forever's PvP is at its best when the Alliance and Horde are on equal footing, and we are dedicated to helping maintain that balance so that we can all witness battles at the epic scale that has made WoW: Forever PvP so memorable thus far," Blizzard said.

One week after WoW: Forever's shockingly smooth launch , we've been impressed how visual updates and Blizzard's changes to the classic WoW formula have made the MMO feel brand new again . Forever received its first major class and dungeon changes earlier this week.

The Legend of Zelda games are filled with puzzles for Link to solve. Now there’s a Zelda-themed puzzle for you to solve outside of the games, in real life. This Triforce puzzle is comprised of four interlocking metal pieces. Your job is simply to figure out how to slide the pieces around to take them apart. Then, once you have the puzzle disassembled, you can try to re-assemble it.

items.title: 八位堂 Ultimate 3E 无线控制器评测
items.summary: Is Xbox wireless connectivity and modularity really worth that price?

content.v: Pricing has remained the elephant in the room for almost all PC Gaming hardware this year, but when it comes to controllers, you don't even have the memory crisis to blame.

And yet, I feel similarly about the 8BitDo Ultimate 3E as I do all that memory-equipped hardware: This is genuinely an excellent gamepad that I have loved reaching for every day, but that price stings so badly that it becomes quite hard to recommend.
Unless, of course, you really want a dual-compatible (Xbox and PC) modular wireless controller.
Buy if…

✅ You want the best wireless pad for your Xbox: The Ultimate 3E acts exactly like the standard Microsoft Xbox controller, even waking up the console with the on button, except it's better in almost every way.
Don't buy if…

❌ You want the best value for money: You can get the GameSir G7 Pro, with its tri-mode connectivity and charging stand for nearly half the price. Add ten bucks to the G7 Pro, and you can even get its 8K variant.
Features
Layout
Asymmetrical
Thumbsticks
TMR
Gyro
6-axis gyroscope
Connectivity
Tri-mode for PC and Xbox. Bluetooth for Mobile
Battery
1400 mAh, 18-hour playtime
Polling Rate
1,000 Hz (250 Hz on Xbox)
Dimensions
Weight
Price

This isn't just a PC controller that works wired on an Xbox, like most controllers. This is an officially licensed product with Microsoft's coveted wireless chip inside, meaning it works wirelessly on Xbox and PC. Not only that, but it even wakes up the Xbox when you click the On button, effectively doing what the standard Xbox controller does. This may not seem like a big deal, but it's shockingly rare among third-party controller manufacturers right now.

To swap between PC and Xbox, you just have to swap the adapter between the two. Given the price, I'd really love two adapters, as the Turtle Beach Stealth Pro II has, but it's not a huge pain, and the controller has Bluetooth and wired connectivity.

In addition to coming with a charging dock, carry case, and USB Type-A to Type-C cable, the case comes with spare thumbsticks, face buttons, and a D-pad. That's because the Ultimate 3E is modular. You can take off the faceplate and swap around the parts above in mere moments. It's intuitive, and all the parts are built well.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/bqjGC4EjkHYXcSHQ7SvZV5-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Jvy6Q63CtP9FW4njDdUgR6-1920-80.jpg

You also get more modern controller upgrades, like TMR joysticks, two buttons at the back and two extra buttons on top. It does do away with some of my criticisms of the 8BitDo Pro 3 by giving you a 1,000 Hz polling rate and an aux jack, but even then, I would have hoped for 8,000 Hz at this price point. Admittedly, most players won't use 8,000 Hz polling given its battery-sucking ways, but you'd still expect a pro-level controller to have everything thrown at it.

The main difference between the Ultimate 3 and Ultimate 3E is that the 3E comes with RGB rings around the sticks, has rubberised grips at the front and back, and, of course, modular parts. The 3E is also heavier.

As far as modularity is concerned, it's very easy to do. For the thumbsticks and D-pad, you can simply pull them until they pop off, and then slot in the replacement. The face buttons are a little more involved, with you needing to take the faceplate off, pinch the two sides of the face button module and pull. From here, you can swap with the included face button module in the carry case, which is identical except it comes with mechanical switches.

It seems unlikely you will use this modularity every day, but this level of customisation is certainly welcome to me, and does make the controller feel unique. Unfortunately, though, it doesn't opt for any peculiar modules, like the Victrix Pro BFG Reloaded , which does feel like a slightly wasted opportunity.

Given it works on PC and Xbox, I'd love a touchpad module option. The Victrix even gives you the option to change the stick layout, which the Ultimate 3E doesn't. There are levels of modularity on controllers, and the Pro BFG Reloaded is one level above.
Ergonomics

At 285 grams, the 8BitDo Ultimate 3E is around 10 grams lighter than the standard Xbox controller, and it feels super sturdy and comfortable in the hands. The Ultimate 3 and 3E are slightly larger than the Ultimate 2, and I can comfortably say this is the sweetest 8BitDo controller I've held. It's impeccably well-balanced and smoothly slots into my palms. All of its buttons are easy to get to, and surprisingly, I even found myself using the two extra buttons near the bumpers. 8BitDo clearly knows how to make a great-feeling controller.
If I really shake it, the controller has a slight rattle in the centre, but I never heard that in the course of usual play.

It's not failed me once in its connectivity; buttons are snappy and precise, and it doesn't fatigue me after hours of bad luck in the game.
More recently, it's been my way of playing Warhammer Survivors , a very chill game where you constantly hold down the thumbsticks, and these TMR sticks are impressive—precise and smooth.

The best word I can use to describe the Ultimate 3E is clean. Well, not after my hands get on it, but we'll get to that later. The 3E comes in a suave black model, with almost every element of the pad being a shade of black. The only thing cutting through that lack of colour is the LED around the on button and the RGB sticks. Simply click the start button to turn on the RGB, and hold it while using the D-pad to change colour, vibrancy and mode.

It reminds me of a souped-up version of Nintendo's Pro Controller, and that is a big compliment in my eyes. The Ultimate 3 does have some gorgeous colourways, but if you want something simple yet pretty, the 3E is great.
The same can be said for the stand, which is all black with a small RGB strip which doubles as a way of telling you if your controller is charging.

However, there is one blemish here: the grips can get grubby. I've been using GameSir's G7 Pro 8K for almost half a year now and I haven't managed to get its grips quite as mucky looking at the 3E. It certainly doesn't look awful with a speck of dust or grime on the grip, but it does look less clean in both senses of the word.
Software

For the Ultimate 3E, 8BitDo uses the Ultimate Software X, which is the same software it uses for Xbox devices. This is mildly annoying as I use the standard Ultimate software for my Retro keyboard and Retro R8 gaming mouse, meaning I can't use one bit of software for all three.

With this software, you can customise the range and rumble of the triggers, the deadzone of sticks, and get firmware updates. It's fairly straightforward, though after the initial setup, you can do most of the everyday customising without software, including setting controls to the extra buttons, adjusting RGB, and even changing volume.

content.v: Earlier this year, during the Overwatch Spotlight in which Team 4 promised a different approach to managing the live service game, 10 heroes were teased. Five were released straight away , with Sierra, Shion, D.Mon, and Doctrine all being added to the game in subsequent seasons. This has left just one hero for the last season of the year, who also just so happened to be the hero I was most excited about back when the Spotlight was released.

But good things come to those who wait, and now after the better part of a year we finally know more about this final hero. His character design was shown at BlizzCon, which showed him to be omnic detective (my hype was well placed), but now we also know that he'll be joining the DPS class in season 6, although that wasn't always the plan.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/hq2QSC3tZyH6x9L9qbwn3-1920-80.png

"Back at Spotlight—I forget who I was talking to—we said we were going to do a support in season 6," associate game director Alec Dawson said during a stream with Flats and Emongg . "And originally that was the plan. But as things developed as the hero developed, as we got to mechanics, how they matched with the aesthetic, how they matched with who the hero is supposed to be," things changed. The decision was ultimately taken to switch him to the DPS role. "I don't know what else I'm allowed to say," Dawson adds. "I'll let Aaron [Keller, game director] say anything else."

"We'll just spill it all," Keller says, and that he does. "Megan just slacked that we've said enough but there's a couple of other things that I want to say about him. One of the cool things about this, so there was like a bit of a pivot on Hudson (accidentally leaks his name), oh whoops." Well there it is folks: the omnic detective is called Hudson, a cool name for a cool dude, it all checks out.

Hudson's Role Change Explained in #Overwatch 🔎He was initially planned as a Support hero, but as development progressed, the team realized the core mechanic people loved most fit the DPS role better.The hero set record scores in research groups. https://t.co/VxTMpsPLUr November 13, 2026

As a support main I am a little sad to hear about this change to DPS, but seeing as Team 4 explained how they "leaned into the things we loved the most about this hero and it definitely fit DPS a lot better", I'm happy with the change. I'll just have to put support aside for a couple of months, because there's no way I'm missing out on this hero.

This isn't just because he looks cool; according to Keller, Hudson is the most popular hero to-date among their internal and external testers: "We're always testing stuff and we have a user research group here and we'll bring in external players and stuff like that, and this hero by far got the highest scores of any hero that we've tested with these groups. I think he's so much fun."

To put this into perspective, the second most popular hero among testers within the last few years is Juno; a hero I would consider to be one of the best in recent Overwatch history. Her kit is fun, intuitive, and gels with her character design. So if that's the bar Hudson has beaten then my excitement is yet again very well placed. Oh, and Dawson says "he has a very fun accent", which really seals the deal for me.

items.summary: Nintendo is celebrating The Legend of Zelda's 40th anniversary in many different ways, but one detail on the c

content.v: Nintendo is celebrating The Legend of Zelda's 40th anniversary in many different ways, but one detail on the company's official website raised confusion--and curiosity-- about a classic 3DS Zelda game.

A "History" page on Nintendo's website lists every mainline Zelda game in release order, including the release date and which platforms you can play for each entry. The site marks every game that's playable for Nintendo Switch Online subscribers--and the 2013 3DS game The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds was marked as such. The NSO icon has since been removed from the site.

Currently, the Nintendo Classics library allows NSO subscribers to play select NES, SNES, and Game Boy games, while the Expansion Pack subscription includes access to Nintendo 64, Game Boy Advance, GameCube, and Virtual Boy games. There's currently no way to play 3DS games on Nintendo Switch, prompting the question of whether this was an error on Nintendo's website or an accidental leak that A Link Between Worlds will somehow be playable on Switch. GameSpot has reached out to Nintendo for clarification on the matter.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Screenshot-2026-11-13-113221.png

The site appropriately labels the Zelda games featured on Nintendo Classics if they are only playable with the Nintendo Switch Online Expansion Pack subscription, which applies to Ocarina of Time ( the original ), Majora's Mask, A Link to the Past/Four Swords on GBA, The Wind Waker, and The Minish Cap.

If this labeling for A Link Between Worlds were true, it would be surprising if the Expansion Pack were not required to play it. Nintendo Classics also lacks any Wii or DS games, so jumping straight to 3DS would be a bizarre move for the service.

Whatever the case, A Link Between Worlds is a magnificent entry in the Zelda series that deserves to be experienced. GameSpot's 9/10 review of the game called it an "absolute treat to play" with some of the "best Zelda dungeons in years."

items.title: 热咖啡争议 22 年后，英国政客表示《侠盗猎车手 6》是“我们真正值得自豪的东西”
items.summary: My, how times have changed.

content.v: It's fascinating how things change. I. for instance, used to love staying up all night playing videogames; now I get mad at the world if I miss my bedtime by 10 minutes. In kind of a similar vein, Grand Theft Auto was once the poster child for everything insidious, dangerous, and downright wrong about videogames, but now we have a member of the UK government—a secretary of state, no less—talking about how the upcoming Grand Theft Auto 6 is something the whole country should be proud of.

"My love for videogames knows no bounds, and I am an avid addict of things like Animal Crossing and the Mario series," Lisa Nandy, the UK's secretary of state for digital, culture, media, and sport, told The Rundown. "I'm not sure I get away with taking a day off to do it, but I think it's something that we can be really proud of.

"One of the reasons that we're investing in arts and music and all of those things that give people the chance to live richer, larger lives is because we are creating jobs in these incredible industries. And if you want to make a videogame like Grand Theft Auto, you need animators, you need musicians, you need so many people from across the creative industries to make them work. And why shouldn't it be our children in our communities who get the chance to get those jobs?"

I'm as politically cynical as most folks, and sure, Nandy is using the moment opportunistically to promote her government—although, cynicism notwithstanding, I do respect her ability to stay on-message by turning a softball question about GTA 6 into talking about job creation.

At the same time, though, this is a remarkable turnaround from, say, 20 years ago, when everyone in a position of authority lost their minds over the Hot Coffee mod for GTA: San Andreas. Some of you might not be old enough to remember (you have no idea how much it pains me to say that) but referring to GTA as a legitimate cultural export in the early 2000s would've got any mainstream Western politician laughed out of the room—and suggesting that it'd be cool if the children ( the children! ) grew up to make more games like that? Pure political suicide.

As PC Gamer's Evan Lahti wrote in 2017 , "Any American who played games in the '90s remembers the period of pearl-clutching and pseudoscientific fear-mongering from senators like Joe Lieberman, who led a call to ban violent videogames." This was serious stuff back then, and it wasn't really until the US Supreme Court ruled that videogames, like other creative works, are protected speech under the First Amendment that the hysteria and hand-wringing started to meaningfully die down.

But now here we are, 15 years later: The Miami Heat are cosplaying as a Vice City sports team , Rockstar is holding a huge GTA music festival featuring Cardi B and Travis Scott , half the state of Florida is embracing a Leonida transformation (and the cops aren't even mad about it ), and now we've got the UK government saying it's all quite grand— splendid , even. Time, man. It really is a river carving the bedrock of our souls.

items.summary: When Metal Gear Solid 2 launched 25 years ago it seemed almost indecipherable. Today, it's clear that Kojima's

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/13/mgs2-retrospective-1794582279618.jpg
This is an IGN opinion piece from Carlos Morales. He’s a long-time fan of the Metal Gear franchise and is an advocate for video games as an artform.

Metal Gear Solid may not be the biggest franchise nowadays, but it was one of the pillars of the first three PlayStation console generations. The adventures of the legendary Solid Snake and his counterparts were not just some of the most critically acclaimed and financially successful games on their respective platforms – they also stand as fantastic and emotional works of art. And what a game Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty is, marking its 25th anniversary this year as somehow having become only more relevant and timely now than it was upon its original release on November 13th, 2001.

Series creator Hideo Kojima may have since moved on to new IPs like Death Stranding and his upcoming espionage action game Physint, but the iconic game director’s narrative idiosyncrasies and uncanny ability to predict how society will develop have rarely felt as fully formed as they do in Metal Gear Solid’s first PlayStation 2 entry. Let’s take a look at why MGS2 was so ahead of its time.
Raiden High

To understand MGS2’s place in contemporary culture, we first have to look at it in a historical context. It may be hard to remember now after so many years of reappraisal, but MGS2 proved somewhat divisive on its initial release. The game received excellent reviews and sold more than seven million copies , but it also attracted controversy for its choice of protagonist and its convoluted storyline. Many fans were upset that most of the game was spent playing as new hero Raiden instead of Snake, and that the game was full of long cutscenes and Codec calls where characters spoke at length about philosophical and sociological issues. In a world that was still getting used to constant internet access becoming more prevalent and was uncertain about what social changes the digital age would bring, MGS2 was a complex game that many in the gaming space, both consumer and professional, didn’t know how to process.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/13/mgs2-raiden-1794581693836.jpg

Even IGN’s Ed Lewis said as much in his review of Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater back in 2004, writing that MGS2’s story was of little interest “unless you really want to spend a couple of late, smoky nights going over the details and putting all the pieces together, and they do fit together. While that's kind of interesting if you want a pleasant mind rutting, it was far from fun to watch a game eat itself.”

But time has been kind to MGS2, because many of the topics Kojima explored in the game would become more relevant in the years that followed. The ways social media, the proliferation of digital misinformation for political purposes, and the normalization of automated warfare, deep fakes, and generative AI would turn rifts between demographics into chasms and create a society where many have a tenuous grasp on what reality even is , were all predicted years in advance by Kojima’s landmark title.

MGS2 is a dense text, and such works can need time to digest. Raiden may have irritated some players in 2001, but he’s now generally accepted as a worthwhile protagonist in his own right by series fans, although it probably doesn’t hurt that Metal Gear Solid 4 turned him into a badass cyborg ninja. People interested in video games as an artform have often pointed to MGS2’s thematic depth , with the game’s story exploring ideas like social engineering, digital censorship, cyberwarfare, and post-truth society. If you just want a tactical espionage adventure with big twists, stealth gameplay, and epic boss fights, the game delivers on those expectations. Yet players embracing MGS2’s more cerebral attributes has made the game an enduring phenomenon even a quarter century later.
One attribute in particular, its metatextual use of game design elements as part of its storytelling, is a big part of why it’s such an impressive artistic achievement.
Game Plays You

MGS2 opens with a prologue featuring series protagonist Solid Snake infiltrating a tanker in the Hudson River to gather evidence of a new Metal Gear prototype named Ray. His ill-fated mission results in the ship sinking, Metal Gear Ray being stolen by recurring villain Revolver Ocelot, and Snake assumed dead. Fast forward two years to a facility called the Big Shell having been built where the tanker sank, which has been taken over by terrorists called Dead Cell and an army of Russian mercenaries under the command of Solidus Snake, one of Snake’s evil clones. They have the President hostage and are seeking to launch a nuclear strike. Raiden, a new agent of FOXHOUND (the same outfit Snake used to work for), is ordered to rescue the hostages and stop the terrorists. Sounds like a standard setup, but it’s not too long into Raiden’s mission that it becomes obvious something is amiss.

Raiden’s mission to the Big Shell has numerous parallels to Snake’s infiltration of Shadow Moses in Metal Gear Solid 1, with repeated plot events, scripted sequences, and character appearances. As the game goes on, the player learns that the entire incident has been orchestrated by a shadow group known as the Patriots, who have covertly controlled the United States government for decades. They’ve also controlled Raiden’s life for years, with his girlfriend Rosemary (who also saves the game for you) being a Patriot agent. The allusions to Shadow Moses are intentional, part of an artificial intelligence simulation system designed to control human behavior and generate desired outcomes. Kojima explicitly makes this plot twist a metaphor for how video game players are conditioned to perform certain actions by subconsciously responding to design choices, with most linear, narrative driven games like the MGS series giving players little to no choice but to do exactly what the developers intend.

Kojima’s metatextual take on the mechanics of game design predates similar attempts to tie player agency (or lack thereof) into the storytelling of games like BioShock or Spec Ops: The Line. Later levels draw attention to simulational and constructed aspects of video game structure, such as the reveal that the Colonel who Raiden has been taking orders from all game long is one of the Patriots’ AIs, or a big fight on an elevator trying to trick players with a fake Mission Failed screen. Even the environments themselves become less “real” inside the cavernous halls of Arsenal Gear, the flying fortress the terrorists seek to use. The levels have a similar design and color scheme to the VR training missions from the first game, and the room where Raiden battles a fleet of Metal Gear Rays is a surreal space that seems to go on for eternity.

These and other parts of Metal Gear Solid 2 are as interesting to experience now as they were on release. Yet the area where the game is most relevant in 2026 is how it reflects the distorted reality of the mid-2020s.
He Tried To Tell Us

It’s strange to play a video game from 2001 and see it predict the last decade of social upheaval. The gears of late-stage capitalism in the digital age have seen information control and cultural mythology become the most important weapons of the ruling class. In much the same way that the Patriots seek to restrict the free flow of information using the AI system known as GW, so too have the real world military industrial complex and ruling government bodies weaponized social media, digital news distribution, and automated misinformation infrastructure to make it harder to tell what is real or not to suit the interests of the powers that be. The rise of generative AI has done untold damage to the social contract and our ability to believe literally anything we see online, which is not a great development in a world where not using the internet is no longer really an option.

items.title: 《WoW Forever》每周任务最高奖励 100 金币，但玩家不喜欢
items.summary: Just a couple days after Blizzard changed the way gold was earned in max-level quests WoW Forever, the company

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/09/19/forever-1789805930640.png

Just a couple days after Blizzard changed the way gold was earned in max-level quests WoW Forever, the company has implemented a weekly quest with loot-box-style gold reward. And players don't love it .

Max level players have found a quest in Booty Bay called 'In Demand - Ancient Elven Curiosities,' which is offered each week, according to Wowhead . There is potential that the quest will rotate to different high level dungeons, but so far, for the two weeks Forever has been out, it's pointed players at Dire Maul, where they have to collect three items. The quest rewards a little bag that can drop one of four items at random that are worth either 10g, 20g, 40g, or 100g.

But while this is a way to get gold in a game where money is scarce, it is rubbing a lot of players in the community the wrong way. For a lot of people, it reminds them of retail WoW, which is built on top of piles and piles of weekly quests to pump additional gold into the economy.

WoW YouTuber Bellular posted the Wowhead link on X / Twitter, captioned simply by "uh what," and followed that up with some criticisms of the new weekly quest. He said: "Retail slop, kill! The way to generate gold is crafting, gathering, selling items. Want to do UBI? Make it sneaky via those means. Don’t show the hand of the designer so clearly." Bellular then tagged Blizzard associate production director Clayton Stone and added: "(pardon the spicy language - some genuine feedback) Let the player earn organically through game systems, not by making content a hoop to jump through."

But it's not just Bellular who's upset at the weekly quest. It's a similar sentiment over on Reddit, where ThatOldGuy7863 simply said : "dear god not weeklys." Meanwhile, drtakhs added: "F**k weeklies and dailies. I’ve been pretty happy with all the decision so far and the thought process behind them was reasonable. Now, what is this? Who wants this? No dailies, no weeklies and no FOMO bulls**t are among the most important things that make classic feel… well like classic…"
However, there may be an explanation for Blizzard's move here. EvadableMoxie suggested a repeatable quest for 100 gold "is aggressively anti-bot."

"It reduces the biggest benefit that bots have, the ability to run 24/7 by frontloading gold rewards," the continued. "This of course does not make bots useless but it reduces their advantage while letting players focus on other things than grinding out gold."

Blizzard has long struggled with bots messing with the economy in every version of World of Warcraft. In the beta, the company had to come down hard on people who were buying and selling gold, which is a direct consequence of botting. Simply put, it's not hard to program a bot to crawl zones for you and gather mining, herbalism or other materials to sell en masse on the auction house. A weekly quest that rewards gold could help players that don't have the time to compete with bots dumping industrial amounts of crafting materials keep up.

But players aren't mad that Blizzard is adding a way to earn gold. Rather, it's the addition of a weekly quest, that encourages players to log on every single week for fear of missing out on an injection of gold. This sort of repeatable quest also wasn't in the original game, with most types of daily and weekly quests not being added until The Burning Crusade.

This is just the latest change as Blizzard tries to nail down the identity of WoW Forever. While there are some parts of the original game that the company has stood firm on, like group tagging , there is an ever growing list of gameplay systems that Blizzard is actively tweaking in Forever, like Dungeon Experience and now, gold rewards.

items.title: 专家表示，GTA 6 和其他游戏的 80 美元价格是合理的
items.summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 finally releases on November 19, and you'll have to pay at least $80 for it. Tha

content.v: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 finally releases on November 19, and you'll have to pay at least $80 for it. That's a full $20 more than what GTA 5 cost in 2013 and $10 more than many other big AAA games today. Is $80 going to become the "new normal" for AAA games, or is it, along with Nintendo's Mario Kart World and Tears of the Kingdom for Switch 2 , an outlier at $80?

According to Alinea Analytics researcher Rhys Elliott , $80 won't be an across-the-board new price for all games. Some developers will purposefully price their games lower to draw in more consumers--he pointed to games like Expedition 33 ($50), Phantom Blade Zero ($60), and Oblivion Remastered ($50) as examples.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Ambrosia_06_a679c3.jpg?w=636

Elliott said that when GTA 6 inevitably becomes a huge success with its $80 and $100 editions, some publishers will be "jumping for joy" because they'll take this as a signal that the market will indeed accept these higher prices.

However, Elliott said he hopes the industry doesn't learn the wrong lessons from GTA 6 and its $80 price point. "GTA 6 is as inelastic as things get in entertainment. People will pay anything to get their mitts on this one, which makes it seem like the perfect Trojan horse for an industry-wide price rise," he said.

"The $80 price point will be a Godsend to some publishers, but it’ll be a snowball's chance in hell for others. After all, this kind of stuff can be zero-sum. When a player spends $100 on GTA 6, their remaining budget shrinks," he added.

Elliott went on to list off some of the studios and game franchises that could likely get their fanbases to buy in at $80. He said these include the next big God of War game after Laufey, the next Naughty Dog game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, and future Forza titles (assuming Xbox strips them out of Game Pass). Additionally, Elliott said From Software "has the cache" to charge $80 for its new games, while Hogwarts Legacy 2 could also up the price to $80. Elliott added that some of the top sports games could charge more, but that might be a tougher sell considering those games are full of microtransactions already.
"So not all games were created equal, and mid-tier AAA publishers--and also bigger publishers offering smaller games or remakes--will price downward at $40-$60," Elliott said.

There are a lot of factors at play here. For starters, GTA 5 launched at $60 back in 2013, and that same $60 is worth $86 today after inflation, making GTA 6--at least its $80 edition--effectively cheaper than GTA 5 .

At the same time, many people are acutely aware that their pay has not kept up with inflation, while the federal minimum wage hasn't moved up since 2009. GTA 6 is also coming out at a rough time for many people, with gas and grocery prices surging , and the cost of everyday goods generally spiking due in part to increasing inflation. And anyone heading to a store to buy a console to play GTA 6 on is in for some serious sticker shock, as game consoles today are more expensive than ever due to the AI craze.

New video games generally staying the same price over the years has had serious negative effects on the entire industry, experts have said. It's part of the reason why publishers now try to squeeze people more with DLC, battle passes, microtransactions, collector's editions, paid early access, and more. Recently, an Xbox advertising chief said price increases would be a hard sell, so the company is turning to ads to help offset ballooning budgets and keep the business healthy.

content.v: Skin distribution seems to be an issue in pretty much any game with more than one hero and clear favourites. Marvel Rivals has come under fire for it for a while now, ever since players got wise to which heroes were favourites and which had clearly been shoved to the side.

It all came to a head a few months ago when the summer skins were released, and it was revealed that Storm was the only female hero to not get a legendary costume among all the swimsuit designs. Players did not look upon this favourably , as Storm is a hugely popular character and had already gone a long time without the same kind of legendary skins as other heroes like Luna Snow and had been passed over for skins in the Disco and Egyptian God skin lines.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/cignQhCHEH2w3ijWjM9BmY-1920-80.jpg

But all the player complaints seem to have gotten through to NetEase, with creative director Guangyun Chen acknowledging in a dev diary that "season 10 has been a challenging one for us." Not only were players upset about only one hero being released this season, but the devs have "been closely following the community's feedback regarding certain heroes receiving fewer costumes. With strong demands for more high-quality Legendary costumes featuring recolours and ultimate ability visual upgrades."

The decision has since been made to upgrade Storm's summer skin to legendary tier with the devs "targeting a release around Christmas this December" for it. Other slightly forgotten heroes who will be getting some visual upgrades include Human Torch, who will get a legendary costume in early December which includes "recolours and ultimate ability VFX". Cloak and Dagger will also be getting a (presumably Valentines Day-themed) skin in February.

"We've been hard at work at this for almost eight months," Guangyun Chen says. "Cloak's design will include full legs. We fully re-animated Cloak's entire movement set strictly for this, we really hope you enjoy it."

But with all these new redesigns and costumes on the way, Guangyun Chen wants to remind players that skins can't just be made or changed at a moment's notice: "Please understand that art asset production requires a certain lead time and simply can't be done overnight. Generally, a single costume takes eight to 10 months to produce from start to finish."

Storm's redesigned summer skin has been in the works for three months already, with the finished product coming out after five months of work. That's under the average of eight to 10 months, but this sounds like the exception not the rule.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/02/19/crop-image-project-2-1771515719569.png
Sony has revealed that God of War Sons of Sparta is coming to PS4 next week, and it's bringing two new modes with it.

The unexpected update for this year's action platformer prequel was announced in a PlayStation.Blog post today. In it, Sony confirmed plans to bring Kratos' earliest adventure to the last-gen console starting midnight local time November 16.

It's more than a surprise bonus platform, too, as developer Mega Cat Studios has promised two new modes that will be available on both PS4 and PS5: Hermes Mode and Erebus Mode. The former is described as a "race against the clock" that features speedrunning tools like a split-based timer and a persistent scoreboard. The latter is a one-hit-kill mode that affects both Kratos and his enemies.

Sony and Mega Cat tell God of War Sons of Sparta players that they'll be able to select their mode when starting a new game and selecting a save slot. Game modes can't be changed once selected. Hermes Mode, specifically, is activated only after beating the game once through and after players input the following code: Up, Up, Down, Down, Left, Right, Left, Right, L1, R1, Touchpad. It's unclear if unlocking Erebus Mode has a similar old-school cheat code-esque requirement.

God of War Sons of Sparta takes one of PlayStation's most popular exclusive franchises and scales it down to let players control Kratos at a much, much earlier point in his life in ancient Greece. Shadow-dropped back in February of this year as an experimental chapter of the story for PS5, its story returns to an era fans have longed for with original Kratos actor Terrence 'T.C. Carson back in the booth.

"Every legend has a beginning – before he was a God, before he was a father, Kratos was a young Spartan!" an official story description said. "Experience an untold chapter in Kratos’ journey set during the harsh years of Spartan training alongside his brother Deimos. Through endless trials, their minds, bodies, and hearts have been molded to become Spartan soldiers for whom duty and honor mean everything. After a fellow cadet goes missing, Kratos and Deimos vow to find him and embark on an adventure that will put their training and Spartan spirit to the test."

God of War Sons of Sparta was unable to generate the same level of hype the series' more recent entries have been known for. Despite the surprise of getting a new God of War game without any of the build-up, the prequel side-scroller generally received middling reviews from critics and fans. IGN gave it a 6/10 , calling it "a pretty mediocre Metroidvania" that failed "to meet the high bar set by the titans of the genre."

Franchise creator David Jaffe was less than impressed with God of War Sons of Sparta when it launched. In a video posted at the time, he said a 2.5D God of War game is "the kind of game I've always wanted" but ultimately said it was an experience he did not like and did not recommend. He even went as far as to say, "This is not God of War."

"I wanted to make a video more about what are they thinking, like what the f*** were they thinking?" Jaffe explained. "It's not a bad game by any means, it's fine, it controls decently... but to me the more fascinating part of this is, why is this in existence? I don't understand."

Like it or not, God of War Sons of Sparta offered a stopgap for Sony as it chipped away at the series' next major new entry: God of War Laufey . The PS5-exclusive title is currently set to launch May 20, 2027, following a recent delay . At least the prequel is now available for PS4 users to enjoy while they wait an extra few months.

Pico Park is a fascinating success story for developer Shunsuke Miyake, who created the original game over a decade ago while working at Sega. A cute, minimalist and deceptively challenging puzzler, it exploded in popularity with the introduction of online co-op and a feature-packed sequel that was released on Switch in 2024.

This new spin-off takes the escalating challenge of multiple puzzle modes and invites Sonic and his ever-expanding menagerie of friends to the party. Available on both Switch 1 and 2, Sonic Pico Park takes the core mechanics of Pico Park and adds a suite of design features from the Blue Blur's 16-bit heyday.
